subject: CoralStreet VPC: sudden throughput degradation + spike in 5xx — request for tuning runbook
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@coralstreet.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: infra@coralstreet.com
Date: 2026-12-12T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: CoralStreet VPC experiencing throughput drop and increased 5xx (urgent)

Hi Vivek / Laura,

We started seeing a sustained throughput drop on our CoralStreet private deployment around 14:20 PST. Concurrently our app began returning ~6–8% 500s from the Redwood inference endpoint for ~15–45s windows. Traffic volume was ~30% above baseline due to a promotional push.

Attached is a short excerpt of the logs showing the 500s + a small latency histogram. Can your team advise immediate mitigations we can apply (batching, fallback model, etc.)? We are seeing customer impact.

Quick context: model pinned to rdx-7b-quant, average request length ~220 tokens, QPS peak ~75. This is our private VPC deployment (single AZ), not hosted.

Attachments: coralstreet_latency_log_excerpt.txt (small)

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Director, Platform — CoralStreet
----
On Sun, Dec 12, 2026 at 3:04 PM Samira Khan <samira.khan@coralstreet.com> wrote:
> sending initial logs; will standby for next steps
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@coralstreet.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, dev_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-12T16:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CoralStreet VPC experiencing throughput drop and increased 5xx (urgent)

Samira — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We see the spike in your excerpt. First steps we will take now:

- Reduce default batch size on the pool serving rdx-7b-quant to lower tail latency (temporary, targeted rollout).
- Force fallback to rdx-7b-quant-fast (lower precision variant) if we detect queuing > 25ms.
- Increase concurrent workers by +20% on your Dedicated pool for the next 2 hours while we triage.

Neha (cc) will run a quick queue/backlog analysis and share a perf snapshot. Dev, please prepare a short runbook with exact config knobs we changed so CoralStreet can mirror if they prefer.

I will keep you posted every hour until stable. If this escalates we will schedule an exec sync.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@coralstreet.com>, dev_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-13T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CoralStreet VPC — initial perf triage + artifacts attached

Hi all — initial triage attached (perf_snapshot_20261213.tar.gz). Summary:

- Symptom: short-lived spikes of queue growth and backend 5xx tied to OOM-kernel evictions on one of the inferencer hosts.
- Root contributor (likely): a combination of larger-than-expected input lengths for a subset of requests (~>1k tokens from a campaign), and heavy cache invalidation from prefix diversity causing KV cache thrashing.
- Observed p95 increase from 220ms baseline -> 1.1s during peaks; p99 up to 2.7s.

Immediate mitigations we applied (see runbook_proposed_changes.md):
1) Lowered batch size to 8 for rdx-7b-quant on CoralStreet pool.
2) Enabled stricter prefix-based KV caching for high-frequency routes (experimental flag).
3) Triggered a rolling restart on the evicting host after draining in-flight requests.

Notes / next actions:
- Recommend a model quantization profile change for long-sequence traffic and setting a harder request-length cap or pre-tokenization at the app layer.
- For long term: consider adding one more inferencer host to the pool (burst capacity) and move to multi-AZ for failover.

Attachments: perf_snapshot_20261213.tar.gz, runbook_proposed_changes.md

-Neha
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@coralstreet.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: infra@coralstreet.com, Oliver Brandt <oliver@edgeops.io>
Date: 2026-12-13T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CoralStreet VPC — initial perf triage + artifacts attached

Thanks Neha — this is super helpful. Additional context: the campaign sent a batch of long prompts (avg ~950 tokens) for personalization. We can enforce a client-side truncation, but that will impact output quality.

Oliver (EdgeOps) — can you share whether the network jitter we observed ~13:20 aligns with any maintenance on your side?

We would like Redwood to hold the temporary config changes for the next 24h while we validate. Also please share a concise runbook (one-page) we can hand to our infra team to replicate the mitigations in our environment.

Samira
----

Cc: dev_patel@redwoodinference.com, Samira Khan <samira.khan@coralstreet.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T07:45:00-08:00
Subject: CoralStreet — exec summary & request for leadership sync

Vivek / Neha — quick summary for leadership: CoralStreet hit a customer-impacting throughput regression following a marketing-driven traffic spike combined with unexpected long-sequence requests. SRE mitigations reduced immediate 5xx and brought p95 closer to baseline but the customer is asking for a short runbook they can run themselves and an SLA review (they may request a credit).

Action items for Redwood:
- Produce a one-page runbook for CoralStreet ops (Dev to draft).
- Prepare an internal post-mortem template and proposed credit calculation for potential SLA impact window (Laura to lead).
- Assess cost/benefit of adding burst host vs. moving to multi-AZ for this customer.

Related links: HubSpot:HS-82741, Drive perf artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bCoralStreetPerf

I recommend an executive sync with the CoralStreet CTO if they escalate. Can we target 12/14 11:00 PST? Vivek, can you lead and bring the runbook and current metrics?

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Director — Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@coralstreet.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, dev_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-14T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CoralStreet VPC: throughput degradation + spike in 5xx — next steps and short runbook

Samira — short update ahead of the 11:00 sync:

- Immediate mitigations in place: reduced batch size, enabled prefix-KV cache guard, rolling restart completed on the evicting host. Early telemetry shows 5xx down to 0.8% and p95 improving to ~280–320ms.
- We attached a one-page runbook (runbook_proposed_changes.md) and a short perf snapshot for your ops team.
- Temporary config will remain for 24h; after that we recommend a controlled rollback unless you request otherwise.

Next steps:
1) 11:00 PST sync with CoralStreet CTO (Laura to host).
2) Post-mortem to be shared within 72h with recommended infra changes and a proposed SLA credit (Laura + Finance).
3) Engineering to produce a small QoS policy to refuse >1k token requests for the time being or route them to a long-sequence optimized pool.

Attaching: runbook_proposed_changes.md, perf_snapshot_20261213.tar.gz

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
